next_steps: Send tailored pricing options for 3 reserve tiers
Share SOC2 + KMS architecture doc link
Schedule 60m pilot kickoff & baseline benchmark next Tue 11am PT
Provide short list of model/quantization suggestions for their workload
action_items: Maya: Email pricing and three capacity scenarios by 2026-05-29
Jonah: Prepare benchmark plan and list of telemetry we need by 2026-06-01
Alicia: Share request-for-info (RFI) doc and QPS patterns by 2026-05-30
header:
Date: 2026-05-27
Start: 16:00 PT
Duration: 46 minutes
Attendees: Maya Patel (Redwood AE), Jonah Kim (Redwood SE), Priya Desai (Redwood SE), Alicia Torres (BlueForge - Head ML Infra), Marcus Lee (BlueForge - CTO), Samir Rao (Platform), Helen Wu (Security)
Recorded: yes
Notes: quick product/ops discovery focused on Dedicated (reserved GPUs), tenant isolation, burst/fallback behavior and SLOs.
summary: BlueForge is evaluating Redwood Dedicated for inference serving of a multimodal recommender and a few repo-based LLM features. Primary concerns: strict tenant isolation (regulatory + client contracts), bursty nightly traffic peaks, predictable tail latency for paid customers, and compliance (KMS/SOC2). Team wants a pilot with reserved nodes and a clear fallback policy to hosted models. Action: Redwood to send pricing tiers, SOC2/KMS docs, and propose benchmark plan for a 2-week pilot.
transcript: 00:00 Maya: hey everyone thanks for joining, um we'll do a quick agenda — we're here to understand your constraints around reserved GPUs and surge behavior and figure out a sensible pilot
00:14 Marcus: yeah thanks, um, we appreciate it — quick intro from our side, i'm marcus, cto, we run BlueForge's realtime recommender and some internal LLM features — Alicia will walk through infra

00:26 Alicia: hi all, thanks; i'll piggyback — our biggest thing is tenant isolation, contractually some partners require no co-tenancy and we have to prove encryption at rest, KMS separation; we also have very spiky loads at 2am and 6pm UTC, nightly batch to embeddings and sudden QPS spikes when new content drops
00:46 Jonah: right, so when you say no co-tenancy, do you mean physical isolation on dedicated GPUs or logical isolation with pinned containers?

00:56 Alicia: we prefer physical isolation for a subset of high-value customers — in practice that means dedicated nodes or dedicated node pools that don't share GPUs with other tenants. For lower tiers logical isolation is ok
01:12 Priya: got it, so a hybrid tenancy model — we can map that to reserved node pools + soft-tenant-sharding — we sometimes call the dedicated option a hotpool or reserved pools
01:26 Samir: quick question: what's the prewarm strategy? if we prewarm too many nodes cost explodes, but if we cold start latency is bad — what's the sweet spot?

01:37 Maya: good point, our Dedicated product supports configurable prewarm counts and warm pools, plus autoscaling rules you can set for burst windows — we also support a graceful fallback to the hosted model family if your reserved pool is saturated
01:52 Helen: fallback is a non-starter for some contracts, we need to understand auditability and exactly which data crosses boundaries during fallback — is KMS still customer-managed in that path?

02:05 Jonah: short answer: in Hosted fallback the runtime would use Redwood keying by default; for Private or Dedicated with VPC we support Bring-Your-Own-KMS (BYOK) and HSM integration so keys never leave your control. We'll need to map the fallback path for that contract — i.e., disable automatic fallback for those customers or route to a dedicated spare pool
02:26 Marcus: okay that makes sense. Alicia, i'll flag that as must-have for large partner lane, fallback optional for others
02:34 Alicia: also curious about quantization & model variants — some of our embeddings workloads could run on int8 quantized models to save cost, but we care about accuracy drift

02:46 Jonah: yes we have recommended quantization profiles and we provide regression tests built into Optimize; for embeddings especially, we often suggest a small eval set to measure vector-distance drift — we can share a short doc and example tolerances
03:01 Maya: can you give us rough numbers — how many reserved GPUs you'd expect across seasons, and what's the peak QPS?

03:10 Samir: today on peak we push about 3k qps for the recommender reads across the cluster, but that's spread across ~100 nodes; for the initial pilot we want to reserve a small block, maybe 4-8 A100-ish GPUs, then scale up if the pilot is successful
03:27 Priya: okay 4-8 GPUs for pilot, sounds reasonable. what's your expected p99 latency target for paid customers?
03:35 Marcus: sub-250ms p95 and p99 tail under 600ms for text completions; for embeddings p95 < 100ms — but we can relax for batch jobs

03:45 Jonah: noted. we usually measure token-level latency and model hot-cache behavior — if you need consistent p99 we recommend reserved pools with prewarmed KV caches and pinned kernel selection to avoid jitter
04:00 Alicia: how do you handle cold-cache storms? like when a new release invalidates caches across nodes

04:09 Priya: we have a rolling rollout pattern: canary first on a small subset, then PQ warm-up phase where we keep some nodes pinned to old cache, then switch over. there's also an auto-warm path where the runtime backfills KV caches from recent requests; this is sometimes imperfect for long sequences
04:28 Helen: on compliance: do you provide audit logs at the token/request level? our legal team asks for that
04:36 Maya: yes, Dedicated + Private both include request-level logs and can stream to your SIEM; retention is configurable, and we support encrypted logs at rest with your KMS
04:48 Samir: what about network topology — can we have Dedicated inside our VPC with private peering?

04:55 Jonah: for Private deployments yes; for Dedicated we offer VPC peering for enterprise customers. There's an option to run a private control plane and the inference nodes inside your network with limited egress. We'll capture the specific connectivity requirements in the pilot RFI
05:10 Marcus: pricing — high level, is Dedicated a flat monthly commitment for reserved nodes + usage, or fully usage-based?

05:18 Maya: reserved nodes are committed monthly/annually, with tiered pricing for burst capacity; we can model 3 pricing tiers for you: small pilot (4 GPUs), medium (16 GPUs), large (64 GPUs). Burst is charged based on a short-term rate and we include some burst credits depending on the commitment
05:34 Alicia: would like an example run-rate for our 8 GPU steady state plus 2x nightly peaks to 24 GPUs — rough estimate is fine
05:44 Maya: we'll put that in the pricing sheet — include prewarm costs and some assumptions about utilization. we'll send two scenarios: conservative and optimistic
05:55 Samir: operationally, who owns upgrades and kernel patches? we need a maintenance window plan

06:02 Jonah: Redwood manages runtime upgrades for hosted and dedicated control plane; for Private or self-managed on-prem we provide the package and upgrade guide. For Dedicated, we coordinate windows and provide rollback plans and tracing hooks so you can validate after a rollout
06:17 Helen: any SOC2/ISO stuff you can share now?
06:21 Maya: yes we'll share our SOC2 Type II report and our security pack (I'll drop links). For onsite/on-prem we can do additional audits under NDA
06:30 Marcus: talk through the failover story — if your reserved pool loses capacity, what's the policy? automatic fallback or queueing?

06:38 Priya: there's a policy layer: you can pick prioritize latency (auto-fallback to hosted variants with similar model) or prioritize isolation (queue or reject). For strict SLAs we recommend a shared spare pool or over-provisioning and scheduled burst allowances
06:54 Alicia: hmmm, shared spare pool sounds interesting — how is that billed and can it be reserved just for a tenant?
07:02 Jonah: yes you can designate spare capacity as soft-reserved for specific tenants; billing shows committed + reserved spare plus consumed burst. We'll show the invoicing view in the console
07:13 Marcus: what observability do we get? token-level cost breakdowns? per-route latency?
07:19 Maya: console provides per-route and per-model dashboards, token-level cost, traces, and artifact links for problematic requests. We also integrate with Datadog/Prometheus for metrics export
07:32 Samir: on canaries: if we want to A/B test a quantized variant vs baseline in production, is that supported?
07:39 Priya: yes canary/A-B rollouts are supported; you can route X% to a variant and set automatic rollback if quality regressions exceed a threshold. We tie regressions to prompt sets if you want
07:52 Helen: security: do you support SSO, RBAC, and per-team quotas? we need role separation for auditors
07:58 Jonah: SSO via SAML/OIDC, fine-grained RBAC, and per-token/project quotas are available — audit trail is preserved

08:06 Alicia: ok, good. for the pilot we want to test: 1) 4 GPU reserved pool with BYOK, 2) burst to 16 GPUs during nightly window, 3) no automatic fallback for partner lane, 4) measure p95/p99 and recurrence of cold-cache events
08:22 Maya: agreed. propose 2-week pilot: week1 functional + connectivity, week2 load tests and run benchmarks and regression checks. We'll supply test harness and example requests
08:33 Marcus: timeline — we want pilot in mid-June if possible, procurement ok in early June
08:40 Maya: that'll work; we'll put tentative dates in the follow-up email. any blockers?
08:45 Samir: just ensure we have the exact egress/topology docs; Helen will review security pack

08:52 Helen: yes and also a clear statement on key custody during fallback — if fallback is disabled for partner lane, we need to ensure requests won't be routed to hosted endpoints that use different KMS
09:04 Jonah: we'll include a fallback matrix in the pilot plan that enumerates routing outcomes for each policy and where keys reside
09:12 Alicia: also ask: can we reserve GPUs of specific instance types? some of our models are memory heavy and need 80GB ddr configurations

09:21 Priya: we can reserve by instance family; we'll capture your model memory/seq length and recommend mapping — for memory heavy models we suggest larger instance types or sharded execution. we'll include a mapping doc
09:35 Marcus: any limitations on multi-region? we need EU residency for a subset of customers
09:41 Maya: Dedicated supports region pinning; for EU residency we can allocate reserved pools in eu-west and provide data residency controls. For Private on-prem we avoid egress entirely
09:52 Samir: what's typical lead time to ramp a reserved pool from small pilot to ~64 GPUs?

09:58 Jonah: depends on hardware availability; typically 2-6 weeks for capacity procurement if cloud region has spare capacity; for on-prem it's longer. We'll surface expected lead times in the pricing sheet
10:12 Alicia: let's talk risk: what if we hit a critical bug during the pilot? SLA credits?
10:18 Maya: we'll define an SLA in the pilot agreement and cover operational support during the pilot; for long-term committed contracts SLA and escalation paths are formalized
10:27 Marcus: ok good. been helpful. Any other questions from BlueForge?
10:32 Helen: one more — data retention policies, do you support automatic purge timelines and tenant-level retention?
10:38 Jonah: yes configurable retention by tenant, and we can do short retention for sensitive workloads. We'll add details to the security doc

10:46 Maya: recap — Redwood to send SOC2 + security pack, tailored pricing for 3 commitment scenarios incl prewarm cost, pilot plan and benchmark checklist, and fallback matrix. BlueForge to share RFI with QPS patterns and sensitive tenant list
11:01 Marcus: thanks everyone, we'll review and aim to have procurement signoff first week of June
11:06 Maya: perfect, we'll follow up with calendar invite for pilot kickoff and pricing doc — thanks all
11:12 (call ends)
